papers.title: PoolParty: streamlined design of DNA sequence libraries in Python.
papers.abstract: Computationally designed DNA sequence libraries are essential components of massively parallel reporter assays (MPRAs), deep mutational scanning (DMS) experiments, and other multiplex assays of variant effect (MAVEs). They are also increasingly used in silico to analyze genomic AI models. Designing these libraries, however, remains tedious and error-prone due to the scarcity of purpose-built software.
papers.summary: PoolParty is a new Python package that streamlines the design of DNA sequence libraries for massively parallel reporter assays, deep mutational scanning, and other multiplex assays of variant effect. It addresses the lack of purpose-built software, reducing the tedium and error-proneness of library design, and can also be used in silico to analyze genomic AI models.

papers.title: Assessing the predictive potential of the Holstein bovine sperm methylome for bull fertility using machine learning.
papers.abstract: Bull fertility is a key parameter in the dairy cattle industry, with significant economic implications. DNA methylation is an epigenetic mark essential for fertility, and recent works have highlighted sperm DNA methylation as a promising source of biomarkers for male fertility, but no operational tool has been developed for predicting bull fertility based on DNA methylation. Here, we leveraged existing methylation data to evaluate the potential of DNA methylation for predicting bull fertility with machine learning models.
papers.summary: This study tested whether DNA methylation patterns in Holstein bull sperm can predict bull fertility using machine learning models. Using existing methylation data, the authors evaluated the predictive potential of the sperm methylome as a biomarker for fertility in dairy cattle. The work represents an initial assessment toward developing an operational tool for fertility prediction based on epigenetic marks.

papers.title: Microbiology Galaxy Lab: a community-driven gateway for reproducible and FAIR analysis of microbiological data.
papers.abstract: The explosion of microbial omics data has outpaced the ability of many researchers to analyse it, with complex tools and limited computational resources creating barriers to discovery. To address this gap, we present the Microbiology Galaxy Lab (MGL): a free, globally accessible, community-supported platform that combines state-of-the-art analytical power with user-friendly accessibility. Supported by the Galaxy and global microbiology communities, this platform integrates over 315 tool suites and 115 curated workflows, enabling comprehensive metabarcoding, (meta)genomic, (meta)transcriptomic,
papers.summary: The authors present the Microbiology Galaxy Lab (MGL), a free, community-supported web platform that gives microbiologists access to over 315 tool suites and 115 curated workflows for reproducible, FAIR analysis of metabarcoding, metagenomic, and metatranscriptomic data. The platform aims to lower computational and technical barriers that prevent many researchers from analyzing the rapidly growing volume of microbial omics data.

papers.title: Verix: a toolkit for benchmarking and harmonization of complex structural variants.
papers.abstract: Complex structural variants (CSVs) represent a critical yet under-characterized class of large-scale genomic rearrangements. CSV discovery requires not only the accurate detection of individual breakpoints but also their assembly into a single, structurally resolved CSV event. However, CSV method development is currently limited by a diagnostic gap: existing SV evaluation frameworks are designed for single-interval or single-junction SVs and cannot quantify multi-breakpoint CSV reconstruction fidelity or systematically distinguish between different types of reconstruction errors, such as over-
papers.summary: Verix is a new software toolkit designed to benchmark and harmonize complex structural variants (CSVs), which are large genomic rearrangements involving multiple breakpoints. Existing evaluation frameworks only handle simple single-breakpoint variants, so Verix fills a gap by enabling systematic assessment of how well methods reconstruct multi-breakpoint CSV events and by distinguishing different types of reconstruction errors.

papers.title: MitImpact 4: a genome-wide resource for the interpretation of coding and non-coding mitochondrial DNA variants.
papers.abstract: Mitochondrial DNA variants are a frequent cause of inherited disease, yet their computational interpretation has focused almost exclusively on the 13 protein-coding genes. Variants in tRNA and rRNA genes, which carry a disproportionate share of the known pathogenic alleles, have remained a diagnostic blind spot, because their effect depends on RNA structure rather than on protein sequence and few dedicated predictors exist. MitImpact 4 removes this asymmetry. The database now covers all 49 704 single-nucleotide variants that can occur in the mitochondrial genome and reports their functional co
papers.summary: MitImpact 4 is a database that now covers all 49,704 possible single-nucleotide variants across the entire mitochondrial genome, not just the 13 protein-coding genes. It adds functional predictions for tRNA and rRNA variants, which were previously a diagnostic blind spot because their effects depend on RNA structure rather than protein sequence. This removes a long-standing asymmetry in mitochondrial variant interpretation and provides a genome-wide resource for clinical and research use.

papers.title: Experimental benchmarking of in silico annotations at prostate cancer risk loci and hypothesis-generating cross-cancer prioritisation of ovarian risk variants.
papers.abstract: Genome-wide association studies (GWAS) have identified numerous non-coding risk variants for prostate and ovarian cancers, yet determining which are regulatorily active and which target genes they control remains challenging. We re-analysed a dinucleotide-barcode massively parallel reporter assay (DiR-seq) of 208 bi-allelic prostate cancer risk single-nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) in three prostate cancer cell lines under false-discovery-rate (FDR) control, identifying 50 regulatory SNPs at FDR < 0.10 (30 at FDR < 0.05), including 9 shared by at least two cell lines. Benchmarking standard in
papers.summary: The authors re-analyzed a massively parallel reporter assay (DiR-seq) testing 208 prostate cancer risk SNPs in three cell lines, identifying 50 regulatory SNPs at FDR < 0.10. They then benchmarked standard in silico annotation tools against these experimental results and applied the approach to prioritize ovarian cancer risk variants by cross-cancer comparison. The work provides an experimental benchmark for evaluating computational predictions of regulatory non-coding variants.

papers.title: An Integrated Framework Coupling Hierarchical Hyperspectral i-trait Screening, Gene Identification, and Functional Validation for Genetic Dissection of Salt Tolerance in Cotton.
papers.abstract: Cotton is an economically pivotal fiber crop worldwide, but its growth and yield are critically limited by soil salinity. Salt tolerance is a complex quantitative trait, and conventional destructive phenotyping methods have long hindered the efficiency and accuracy of gene discovery and genetic dissection. To overcome this phenotyping bottleneck and establish a streamlined workflow from phenotype to gene, we developed an integrated framework coupling dynamic hyperspectral phenomics, hierarchical trait selection, genome-wide association study (GWAS), and functional validation, and applied it to
papers.summary: The authors developed an integrated framework that combines dynamic hyperspectral imaging, hierarchical trait selection, GWAS, and functional validation to dissect salt tolerance in cotton. This approach overcomes the limitations of destructive phenotyping, enabling efficient gene discovery for a complex quantitative trait. The workflow provides a streamlined path from phenotype to gene and identifies candidate genes for salt tolerance.

papers.title: Uncovering intergenic DNA i-motifs in the telomere-to-telomere human genome.
papers.abstract: Noncanonical DNA structures such as i-motifs (iMs) are emerging as versatile functional elements within the human genome, yet their distribution and properties outside regulatory regions remain poorly characterized. Leveraging the complete telomere-to-telomere (T2T-CHM13) genome assembly, we generated an updated genome-wide catalogue of putative iM-forming sequences by implementing a bioinformatics pipeline for the systematic detection and statistical assessment of cytosine-rich motifs consistent with canonical iM-forming patterns. The analysis identified 789,952 candidates, representing a 6.3
papers.summary: Using the complete telomere-to-telomere human genome assembly, the authors built a bioinformatics pipeline to catalogue putative i-motif-forming sequences genome-wide, identifying 789,952 candidates—a substantial expansion over prior catalogues. The work highlights that these noncanonical DNA structures are widespread in intergenic regions, not just regulatory regions, broadening the scope of where i-motifs may function.

papers.title: Aircraft and Airport Wastewater Surveillance for Public Health Preparedness Demands an Integrated and Sustainable Approach.
papers.abstract: As domestic and international travel has expanded, the risk of the cross-border dissemination of infectious pathogens has increased, as clearly evidenced during the COVID-19 pandemic. Aircraft- and airport-based wastewater surveillance can provide timely, aggregate evidence of pathogen circulation among mobile populations and may complement clinical, genomic, and syndromic surveillance at points of entry. The strongest evidence for this approach comes from SARS-CoV-2 RNA detection and variant monitoring in aircraft lavatory wastewater, airport terminal wastewater, and airport-associated wastew
papers.summary: This perspective argues that wastewater surveillance at airports and on aircraft can provide early, aggregated signals of pathogen circulation among travelers, complementing clinical and genomic surveillance at borders. The strongest evidence so far comes from detecting SARS-CoV-2 RNA and variants in lavatory and terminal wastewater, but the authors stress that scaling this approach requires integrated, sustainable systems rather than ad hoc pilots.

papers.title: Serial Cryosectioning for the Spatial Transcriptomics of Plant Tissues.
papers.abstract: Spatial transcriptomics enables genome-wide gene expression profiling while preserving tissue architecture, making it a powerful approach for studying plant developmental transitions. However, preparing small and structurally complex plant tissues for spatial transcriptomics remains technically challenging because samples must be rapidly preserved, precisely oriented, serially sectioned, and accurately positioned within the limited capture area of the Visium slides. Here, we describe an optimized workflow for cryo-embedding, serial cryosectioning, section placement, and data analysis of small
papers.summary: This protocol describes an optimized workflow for preparing small, structurally complex plant tissues for 10x Visium spatial transcriptomics, covering cryo-embedding, serial cryosectioning, section placement on capture slides, and downstream data analysis. The method addresses the practical challenges of rapid preservation, precise orientation, and accurate positioning of small plant samples within the limited capture area.

papers.title: Marker-Centered Evaluation of De Novo Assemblers Using Validated Microsatellite Loci in the Endangered Korean Fish Pseudopungtungia nigra.
papers.abstract: The recovery of experimentally validated microsatellite loci from short-read assemblies may provide an application-specific measure of assembly quality that complements conventional genome-wide statistics. In this study, four de novo assemblers-SPAdes, ABySS, SOAPdenovo2, and MaSuRCA-were evaluated using genomic reads from two individuals of the endangered Korean freshwater fish Pseudopungtungia nigra. Assembler performance was assessed based on assembly contiguity, BUSCO completeness, computational requirements, and the recovery of 20 PCR-validated microsatellite loci and their flanking regio
papers.summary: This study benchmarks four de novo genome assemblers (SPAdes, ABySS, SOAPdenovo2, MaSuRCA) on short-read data from the endangered Korean fish Pseudopungtungia nigra, evaluating them not only by standard metrics (contiguity, BUSCO completeness, computational cost) but also by their ability to recover 20 PCR-validated microsatellite loci and their flanking regions. The authors propose that recovery of experimentally validated markers offers an application-specific measure of assembly quality that complements genome-wide statistics. The work provides a practical comparison of assembler performance for a non-model organism of conservation concern.

papers.title: Synthetic Reconstruction and Characterization of Endogenous Bacteriophage Genomes from Desulfovibrio vulgaris.
papers.abstract: Microbiologically influenced corrosion (MIC) caused by sulfate-reducing bacteria (SRB) is a major challenge in industrial infrastructure, yet the limited availability of well-characterized bacteriophages has hindered the development of phage-based strategies for controlling these organisms. Here, we present an integrated genome-guided workflow for the discovery, validation, and synthetic reconstruction of endogenous prophages from the model sulfate-reducing bacterium Desulfovibrio vulgaris Hildenborough. Bioinformatic analysis using PHASTEST identified seven prophage-like regions distributed t
papers.summary: The authors developed a genome-guided workflow to identify, validate, and synthetically reconstruct endogenous prophages from the sulfate-reducing bacterium Desulfovibrio vulgaris Hildenborough, a model organism for microbiologically influenced corrosion. Bioinformatic analysis revealed seven prophage-like regions, and the team demonstrated that these can be revived as functional phages through synthetic reconstruction. This provides a new resource for developing phage-based strategies to control corrosive sulfate-reducing bacteria.

papers.title: Identification of Genes Associated with Gut Microbiota Metabolites in Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus Complicated by Acute Cerebral Infarction Based on Bioinformatics and Mendelian Randomization.
papers.abstract: Background: Type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) and acute cerebral infarction (ACI) are globally prevalent diseases that impose substantial public health burdens. While gut microbiota (GM) is increasingly recognized to regulate metabolic and immune homeostasis linked to both diseases, its shared genetically predicted microbial taxa and underlying metabolite-gene regulatory mechanisms in T2DM and ACI remain unclear, highlighting the need for systematic investigation. Accordingly, this study aimed to elucidate their regulatory mechanisms. Methods: Transcriptomic datasets, genome-wide association stu
papers.summary: This study integrates transcriptomic data with Mendelian randomization to identify gut microbiota taxa and metabolites that may causally contribute to type 2 diabetes complicated by acute cerebral infarction, and links them to candidate genes. It proposes metabolite-gene regulatory axes as shared mechanisms between the two conditions. The work is exploratory and relies on publicly available GWAS and expression datasets.

papers.title: Re-Analysis on GRCh38 with the MANE Select Transcript Resolves Previously Undetected Biallelic ODAD4 Variants in Primary Ciliary Dyskinesia.
papers.abstract: Molecular diagnosis is highly sensitive to the human genome assembly used in a bioinformatics pipeline. Panels designed on GRCh37 (hg19) inherit its exon annotation, whereas transcript standards and interpretation databases are anchored to GRCh38 (hg38); a coding exon absent from GRCh37 can therefore be neither targeted nor analyzed. We describe two unrelated individuals with primary ciliary dyskinesia (PCD) in whom first-line, GRCh37-based panel sequencing was non-diagnostic. Both were re-analyzed on GRCh38 against the Matched Annotation from NCBI and EMBL-EBI (MANE) Select transcript. In Pat
papers.summary: Two patients with primary ciliary dyskinesia whose GRCh37-based panel sequencing was non-diagnostic were re-analyzed on GRCh38 using the MANE Select transcript, revealing previously undetected biallelic ODAD4 variants. The study shows that genome assembly and transcript annotation choices can cause coding exons to be missed, directly affecting molecular diagnosis.

papers.title: Deep Genomic Characterization of Bacillus subtilis SNUY1 & 168 Using MAYA (Multistage Analysis of Prokaryotic Annotations): An Integrated Snakemake-Based Bioinformatics Pipeline.
papers.abstract: Bacillus subtilis is an extensively characterized Gram-positive bacterium with broad applications in agriculture, biotechnology, and biocontrol. Strain SNUY1, known for its antifungal properties and use as an edible coating, has been completely sequenced and deposited in NCBI (accession: CP199918), making it an important model for genomic and functional characterization. Here, we present the MAYA pipeline, a fully automated, rule-based Snakemake workflow that integrates eighteen bioinformatic tools into a single end-to-end framework. MAYA accepts either raw Illumina paired-end FASTQ reads or p
papers.summary: The authors present MAYA, an automated Snakemake-based pipeline that integrates eighteen bioinformatics tools to perform end-to-end genomic annotation and characterization of prokaryotes. They apply it to Bacillus subtilis strains SNUY1 and 168, providing a reproducible workflow for functional annotation of bacterial genomes from raw reads or assemblies.

papers.title: Nanopore Sequencing for Epigenetic Decoding: Applications, Analytical Constraints, and Translational Prospects.
papers.abstract: Epigenetic regulation involves multiple molecular layers, including DNA and RNA modifications, histone post-translational modifications (PTMs), and chromatin accessibility. These processes contribute to cell identity, development, and disease, but their measurement remains technically challenging because sequence context, molecular modification, chromatin state, and transcript structure are often assayed separately. As a representative third-generation sequencing technology, nanopore sequencing is profoundly reshaping the interpretation of the epigenetic code through its distinctive capabiliti
papers.summary: This review examines how nanopore sequencing can decode multiple epigenetic layers—DNA and RNA modifications, chromatin accessibility, and transcript structure—from long native molecules, rather than assaying each separately. It surveys applications across cell identity, development, and disease, while discussing analytical constraints such as base-calling accuracy and modification-detection algorithms, and outlines translational prospects. The paper is a synthesis of an emerging technology rather than a primary data study.

papers.title: A step forward in comprehensive nanopore-based forensic profiling of STRs, InDel, SNP and mtDNA for identity and appearance prediction.
papers.abstract: The targeted analysis of diverse DNA markers, including single nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs), insertion deletion polymorphisms (InDels) and DNA methylation levels, is central to forensic DNA phenotyping, enabling inference of BGA, appearance traits, and age. Such information is relevant when DNA comparison after conventional DNA profiling fails to identify a person of interest. Recent technological developments allow both genetic and epigenetic markers to be analyzed in long-reads within a single platform such as Oxford Nanopore Technologies (ONT). This approach offers an advantage over trad
papers.summary: This study demonstrates a nanopore-based forensic profiling approach that simultaneously analyzes STRs, InDels, SNPs, and mtDNA from long reads to support both identity matching and appearance prediction. By combining genetic and epigenetic markers on a single Oxford Nanopore platform, it offers a more comprehensive alternative to conventional capillary electrophoresis-based profiling. The work represents a practical step toward integrating long-read sequencing into forensic casework.

papers.title: Cell-free DNA fragmentomics and epigenomic profiling in hematologic malignancies: current evidence, translational limitations, and future directions.
papers.abstract: Mutation-based liquid biopsy supports diagnosis and disease monitoring in hematologic malignancies, but interpretation of plasma variants may be complicated by clonal hematopoiesis, treatment-related changes, and nonmalignant blood-cell turnover. This structured narrative review evaluates whether cell-free DNA (cfDNA) fragmentomics, DNA methylation, and 5-hydroxymethylcytosine (5hmC) provide complementary information beyond mutation detection. Direct plasma evidence is most developed for selected fragmentomic and 5hmC applications, although most studies remain retrospective, internally validat
papers.summary: This review examines whether cell-free DNA fragmentomics, DNA methylation, and 5hmC profiling add useful information beyond standard mutation-based liquid biopsy in hematologic malignancies, where clonal hematopoiesis and treatment effects can confound variant interpretation. The authors find that direct plasma evidence is strongest for selected fragmentomic and 5hmC applications, but most studies are retrospective and internally validated only, limiting clinical translation.

papers.title: AI-Assisted WES Variant Interpretation in Neurodevelopmental Disorders: A Narrative Review of Existing Tools.
papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: Neurodevelopmental disorders (NDDs) comprise a heterogeneous group of conditions characterized by alterations in brain development and function, frequently associated with complex genetic architectures. The widespread implementation of next-generation sequencing, particularly whole-exome sequencing (WES), has substantially increased the identification of potentially disease-associated variants, shifting the major challenge from variant detection to their interpretation and prioritization. This review examines the emerging contribution of artificial intelligence (AI) to W
papers.summary: This narrative review surveys how artificial intelligence tools are being applied to interpret whole-exome sequencing variants in neurodevelopmental disorders, where the bottleneck has shifted from variant detection to prioritization and interpretation. It catalogs existing AI-assisted approaches and discusses their role in handling the complex genetic architecture of NDDs.

papers.title: "A human CHRNA6 3' UTR variant alters the molecular environment and microRNA engagement of the adolescent VTA without changing Chrna6 transcript abundance".
papers.abstract: A single nucleotide polymorphism (rs2304297) in the 3' untranslated region (UTR) of CHRNA6, encoding the α6 nicotinic acetylcholine receptor subunit, is associated with adolescent smoking behavior. Humanized rats carrying the "C" or "G" allele show sex- and genotype-dependent responses to adolescent nicotine, yet the variant does not alter the protein sequence and the mechanism has remained unknown. We examined the molecular consequences of rs2304297 in vivo in the adolescent ventral tegmental area (VTA). Chrna6 transcript abundance did not differ by genotype, nor did transcript stability or p
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: This study investigates how a common non-coding variant (rs2304297) in the CHRNA6 3' UTR, linked to adolescent smoking, exerts its effects. Using humanized rats, the authors show the variant does not change Chrna6 transcript levels or stability, but instead alters the local molecular environment and microRNA binding in the adolescent ventral tegmental area. This suggests the variant acts post-transcriptionally through microRNA engagement rather than through gene expression changes.

papers.title: Clinical and Genetic Characterization of a Family with Tooth Agenesis Carrying a Novel LEF1 Variant.
papers.abstract: Background: Tooth agenesis is one of the most common developmental anomalies of the human dentition and may occur either as an isolated trait or as part of a syndromic condition. Advances in genomic technologies have facilitated the identification of genes involved in odontogenesis, including LEF1 (Lymphoid Enhancer-Binding Factor 1), a key transcription factor in the WNT signaling pathway. Methods: Whole exome sequencing (WES) was performed in a proband with non-syndromic tooth agenesis to investigate the underlying genetic cause. Parental segregation analysis was performed through Sanger seq
papers.summary: This study used whole exome sequencing to identify a novel LEF1 variant in a family with non-syndromic tooth agenesis, with Sanger sequencing confirming segregation. The finding adds to the growing evidence that LEF1, a WNT signaling transcription factor, plays a role in human odontogenesis and expands the mutational spectrum for this developmental anomaly.

papers.title: Structural and Molecular Dynamics Analysis of Human β-Defensin 1 Variants Reveals Distinct Perturbation Signatures.
papers.abstract: Human β-defensin 1 (hBD-1) is a small, disulfide-constrained antimicrobial peptide produced predominantly in the kidney and urogenital tract, where it contributes to epithelial innate defense. Genetic variation in the gene encoding hBD-1 has been associated with altered expression levels and susceptibility to infections, including infection following solid organ transplantation, yet the molecular consequences of coding substitutions in the active, mature form remain largely undefined. Here, we integrate conventional genomics, protein bioinformatics, structural modeling, and molecular dynamics
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: This preprint analyzes naturally occurring coding variants in human β-defensin 1, a small antimicrobial peptide important for epithelial innate immunity, using structural modeling and molecular dynamics simulations. The authors report that different substitutions produce distinct perturbation signatures in the peptide's structure and dynamics, offering a molecular rationale for how genetic variation might affect host defense. The work is computational and predictive, with experimental validation not yet described.

papers.title: KmerSignificance score: A discriminative and biologically informed framework for viral k-mer prioritization.
papers.abstract: Distinguishing closely related viral strains requires identifying genomic regions where subtle sequence differences carry biological significance. While k-mer-based approaches offer computational efficiency for genome analysis, existing methods lack standardized frameworks for evaluating which k-mers are most informative. Current selection strategies focus primarily on statistical discriminative power without integrating biological context. We introduce KmerSignificance Score (KSS), a k-mer prioritization framework combining three components: an information-theoretic method measuring strain-di
papers.summary: The authors introduce the KmerSignificance Score (KSS), a framework for prioritizing k-mers that combines statistical discriminative power with biological context to better distinguish closely related viral strains. Unlike existing methods that focus only on statistical discrimination, KSS integrates multiple components to identify k-mers that are both informative and biologically meaningful. This provides a standardized approach for k-mer selection in viral genomics.

papers.title: Conservative evolution of genetic and features in Caenorhabditis becei, an experimentally tractable gonochoristic worm.
papers.abstract: Caenorhabditis nematodes represent a promising model clade for evolutionary genetics and genomics, but research has focused on the three androdioecious species, those with self-fertile hermaphrodites, all in the Elegans Group of species. The majority of Caenorhabditis species are gonochorists, with males and females, characterized by inconveniently high heterozygosity and inbreeding depression. We have identified C. becei as an experimentally tractable gonochorist. We show that transmission-genetic properties known from the androdioecious Elegans Group species are conserved in this Japonica Gr
papers.summary: The authors identify Caenorhabditis becei, a gonochoristic (male-female) nematode, as an experimentally tractable model for evolutionary genetics, addressing the field's heavy reliance on self-fertile hermaphroditic Elegans Group species. They show that transmission-genetic properties known from androdioecious Elegans Group species are conserved in this Japonica Group species, suggesting broader applicability of established genetic tools and approaches.

papers.title: Lysine crotonylation acts as an epigenetic switch for glutamate neurotransmission and spatial memory.
papers.abstract: Histone posttranslational modifications, particularly lysine acetylation (Kac), are critical epigenetic regulators of transcriptional programs underlying long-term memory consolidation. Beyond Kac, several other non-acetyl acylations have been identified with the ability to regulate transcription; however, their role in memory consolidation remains unknown. Here, we identify histone lysine crotonylation (Kcr) as a molecular switch for long-term memory and glutamatergic neurotransmission. We find that spatial learning induces distinct spatiotemporal patterns of Kcr across hippocampal subregions
papers.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America
papers.summary: This study identifies histone lysine crotonylation (Kcr), a non-acetyl histone modification, as an epigenetic switch controlling long-term spatial memory and glutamatergic neurotransmission. Spatial learning produces distinct spatiotemporal patterns of Kcr across hippocampal subregions, suggesting Kcr regulates the transcriptional programs needed for memory consolidation.

papers.title: XenoMix: estimating mouse content from DNA methylation data of Patient-Derived Xenograft models.
papers.abstract: DNA methylation microarrays enable cost-effective, high-throughput profiling of human and mouse samples and are widely used to study epigenetic alterations in cancer. Patient-Derived Xenograft (PDX) models complement this approach by preserving primary tumor characteristics while enabling in vivo studies of drug response and therapy resistance. However, it remains difficult to quantify mouse DNA contamination in PDX DNA methylation data generated using microarrays. We present XenoMix, a light-weight computational tool for quantifying mouse DNA contamination directly from DNA methylation data i
papers.summary: XenoMix is a lightweight computational tool that estimates the proportion of mouse DNA contamination in DNA methylation microarray data from Patient-Derived Xenograft (PDX) models. It addresses the common problem of mixed human-mouse signal in PDX epigenomic profiling, enabling researchers to quantify and account for mouse stromal contamination. This improves the reliability of epigenetic analyses in PDX cancer models.

papers.title: SCCmecExtractor: a tool for extracting staphylococcal cassette chromosome elements from whole-genome sequences.
papers.abstract: Staphylococcal cassette chromosome (SCC) elements are mobile genetic elements that integrate at the rlmH gene and are predominantly responsible for methicillin resistance in staphylococci. Although staphylococcal cassette chromosome mec (SCCmec) typing tools exist, none can extract the element sequence itself or explicitly classify SCC elements that lack methicillin resistance genes. Here, we present SCCmecExtractor, a lightweight Python toolkit that identifies SCC element boundaries through degenerate attachment site (att) pattern matching, extracts complete elements from whole-genome assembl
papers.summary: SCCmecExtractor is a lightweight Python toolkit that identifies the boundaries of staphylococcal cassette chromosome (SCC) elements by matching degenerate attachment site patterns, then extracts the complete element sequences from whole-genome assemblies. Unlike existing SCCmec typing tools, it can also classify SCC elements that lack methicillin resistance genes, filling a gap in mobile genetic element analysis for staphylococci.

papers.title: The Promise and Limitations of Metabolic Trait Prediction Across Diverse Bacteria.
papers.abstract: Metabolic traits mediate microbial interactions and underpin mechanistic models of community assembly. With the rapid expansion of genomic data and bioinformatic tools, it is widely assumed that metabolic traits such as substrate utilization can be reliably inferred from genomes alone. Here, we systematically evaluate this assumption by comparing genome-based predictions from four commonly used tools to high-throughput growth phenotypes of 186 marine bacteria. For simple substrates, prediction accuracy was limited and highly variable across taxa and substrates, with many strains predicted at o
papers.summary: This study tests the common assumption that bacterial metabolic traits, such as which substrates a microbe can use, can be reliably predicted from genome sequences alone. Comparing four popular bioinformatic tools against high-throughput growth phenotypes of 186 marine bacteria, the authors find that prediction accuracy is limited and highly variable across taxa and substrates, especially for simple substrates. The work cautions against over-reliance on genome-based metabolic inference and highlights the need for empirical validation.

papers.title: Long-read sequencing of FLG identifies extensive copy number variation in exon 3 and detects rare loss-of-function variants.
papers.abstract: Loss-of-function (LOF) variants of the FLG gene are risk factors for atopic dermatitis. However, owing to the repetitive nature of exon 3, these variants are difficult to characterize. We sought to determine whether the use of long-read technologies would enable better characterization of the FLG gene and improve the detection of LOF variants. We sequenced a diverse clinical cohort of 192 samples collected in Belgium, Ireland, and Rwanda using long-read sequencing as well as publicly available data. We identified both common and rare LOF variants linked to atopic dermatitis in our clinical coh
papers.journal: JID innovations : skin science from molecules to population health
papers.summary: Using long-read sequencing on a diverse cohort of 192 samples from Belgium, Ireland, and Rwanda, the authors characterized the repetitive exon 3 of FLG, revealing extensive copy number variation and identifying both common and rare loss-of-function variants associated with atopic dermatitis. Long-read technology improved detection of LOF variants that are difficult to resolve with short-read methods.

papers.title: MLMP: A Methylation-Associated lncRNA-mRNA Prognostic Signature for Endometrial Carcinoma.
papers.abstract: Endometrial carcinoma (EC) is one of the most common gynecological malignancies. Aberrant DNA methylation (DNAm) is an important epigenetic alteration involved in cancer progression. Long non-coding RNAs (LncRNAs) play critical roles in gene regulation and pathological processes. However, the biological and prognostic significance of lncRNA-mRNA pairs associated with methylation remains unclear.
papers.summary: This study constructs a prognostic signature for endometrial carcinoma by integrating DNA methylation, lncRNA, and mRNA expression data to identify methylation-associated lncRNA-mRNA pairs. The resulting MLMP model links epigenetic regulation to transcriptomic changes and is evaluated for its ability to predict patient outcomes. It highlights the potential of combined epigenetic-transcriptomic signatures for risk stratification in EC.

papers.title: Epigenetic Insights in Pediatric Multiple Sclerosis: DNA Methylation Highlights an Involvement of Epstein-Barr Virus Infection and Host Immune Networks.
papers.abstract: Pediatric-onset multiple sclerosis (PedMS) provides a unique opportunity to investigate MS pathogenesis because of the short interval between environmental exposures and disease onset. This study aimed to identify differentially methylated regions (DMRs) that mediate the interplay between environmental triggers and genomic factors in the early stages of the disease.
papers.summary: This study identifies differentially methylated DNA regions in pediatric-onset multiple sclerosis patients, revealing epigenetic signatures that link Epstein-Barr virus infection with host immune network dysregulation. The findings suggest that EBV exposure may interact with the host epigenome to contribute to early MS pathogenesis, offering insights from a population where the exposure-to-disease interval is short.

papers.title: Diverse patterns of transcriptional regulation and epigenetic reprogramming within PMDs contribute to ESCC progression by regulating EMT and immunosuppression.
papers.abstract: Partially methylated domains (PMDs) represent extensive genome-wide hypomethylated regions that drive genomic instability and proto-oncogene activation. However, their complex regulatory influence on tumor-specific transcriptional networks remains largely elusive. In this study, we developed a robust computational pipeline to characterize aberrant PMD landscapes across pan-cancer. We specifically focused on the epigenetic features associated with transcriptional dysregulation in esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC). By analyzing gene expression patterns, we classified PMDs into four disti
papers.summary: The authors built a computational pipeline to map partially methylated domains (PMDs) across cancers and applied it to esophageal squamous cell carcinoma, classifying PMDs into four subtypes based on gene expression patterns. These PMD subtypes show distinct epigenetic features and appear to regulate EMT and immunosuppression, linking large-scale hypomethylation to tumor progression.

papers.title: Controlling for DNA dosage with whole-genome sequencing improves ATAC-seq peak calling.
papers.abstract: ATAC-seq is a powerful method for mapping chromatin accessibility and identifying cis-regulatory elements (CREs) across cell types. We reveal that ATAC-seq peak calling is compromised by local biases in DNA dosage, arising from copy number variations but also from DNA replication timing. As part of the FANTOM consortium's efforts, we propose enhancing the model-based analysis of ChIP-seq pipeline by integrating whole-genome sequencing (WGS) data, analogous to input controls in ChIP-seq analyses. This adjustment increases both the number and width of ATAC peaks, with improved proximity to trans
papers.summary: ATAC-seq peak calling is biased by local variation in DNA copy number and replication timing, which can create false or distorted chromatin accessibility signals. The authors show that incorporating whole-genome sequencing data as an input control, analogous to ChIP-seq input controls, corrects for these DNA dosage biases and yields more and wider ATAC-seq peaks that better align with regulatory elements. This work provides a simple methodological improvement for more accurate cis-regulatory element mapping.

papers.title: Assembly and comparative analysis of the mitochondrial genome of Pteroceltis tatarinowii Maxim. (Cannabaceae), a tertiary relict plant endemic to China.
papers.abstract: Pteroceltis tatarinowii Maxim. (Cannabaceae) is a deciduous arbor endemic to China. As a Tertiary relict plant, it is listed as a rare and endangered species under national Class III key protection. Mitochondrial genomic data of P. tatarinowii can improve our knowledge of phylogenetic relationships within Cannabaceae, resolve the taxonomic placement and evolutionary divergence of the genus Pteroceltis, and supply molecular support for conservation and genetic breeding of this endangered tree.
papers.summary: This study assembled and analyzed the mitochondrial genome of Pteroceltis tatarinowii, a rare and endangered Tertiary relict tree endemic to China. The mitochondrial genomic data were used to clarify phylogenetic relationships within Cannabaceae and the evolutionary divergence of the genus Pteroceltis, providing molecular support for conservation and breeding of this species.

papers.title: ogMapper improves speed and memory for short-sequencing read mapping using a novel guided sparse genome index.
papers.abstract: Short DNA-read sequencing has become an everyday essential tool in research and clinical setting. Read mapping is a crucial step that consumes large amounts of memory and CPU time, limiting the hardware required and ultimately restricting its applications. The memory required for the genome index can be approximated as βG, where G is the genome size and β is a factor that depends on the implementation. For example, β ≈ 10 for bwa-mem2 or β ≈ 1.9 for minimap2. Here, an indexing strategy is presented in which β can be even less than 1, commonly around 0.5. The indexing strategy relies on "guides
papers.summary: ogMapper introduces a new genome indexing strategy for short-read mapping that reduces memory usage to roughly half the genome size (β ≈ 0.5), compared to β ≈ 1.9 for minimap2 and β ≈ 10 for bwa-mem2. The approach uses a 'guided sparse' index to lower both memory and CPU demands, making read mapping feasible on less powerful hardware. This could broaden access to short-read sequencing analysis in research and clinical settings.

papers.title: pycircdb: integrated circRNA database annotation for computational workflows.
papers.abstract: Currently, multiple databases exist for the annotation of circular RNAs, providing descriptions of their genomic features, FASTA sequences, predicted microRNA targets and RNA-binding protein interactions. Despite the availability of these resources, annotation remains cumbersome. Conflicting identifiers and genomic coordinates for circular RNAs across databases pose a challenge to reproducibility for users. Furthermore, current databases primarily provide access via web-based graphical user interfaces, bulk downloads and limited programmatic access, rendering their use in computational workflo
papers.summary: pycircdb is a new Python package that integrates multiple circRNA databases into a single programmatic interface, resolving conflicting identifiers and genomic coordinates across sources. It enables reproducible, scriptable annotation of circular RNAs within computational workflows, addressing the current reliance on web GUIs and bulk downloads.

papers.title: vardictcpp: a C++ reimplementation of VarDict variant caller.
papers.abstract: Genomic variant calling is a central computational task in disease research and diagnostics, where somatic mutations such as JAK2 V617F serve as diagnostic markers in myeloid neoplasms. VarDict, originally written in Perl, and its reimplementation VarDictJava are widely used variant callers in the bioinformatics community. The Perl implementation requires run times of up to several hours; VarDictJava reduces this to a few minutes but can consume large amounts of main memory, which limits the number of jobs that can be run in parallel on a given machine. We present vardictcpp, a functionally id
papers.summary: vardictcpp is a C++ reimplementation of the widely used VarDict variant caller, which was originally written in Perl and later reimplemented in Java. It aims to address the slow runtime of the Perl version and the high memory consumption of VarDictJava, enabling more parallel jobs on a given machine. The tool is functionally identical to its predecessors for somatic variant calling tasks.

papers.title: Integrating multi-omics with machine learning: from genomic variant functional annotation to pharmacogenomics and biomarker discovery.
papers.abstract: Integrating heterogeneous multi-omics data with machine learning (ML) provides a powerful framework for interpreting genomic variants and advancing pharmacogenomic research in precision medicine. High-throughput technologies have generated vast datasets spanning genomics, transcriptomics, epigenomics, and proteomics, yet integrating these high-dimensional data into clinically meaningful insights remains a major computational challenge. Machine learning and deep learning models, including Graph Neural Networks (GNNs), Transformers, and Variational Autoencoders (VAEs), offer promising solutions.
papers.summary: This review surveys how machine learning and deep learning models—including graph neural networks, transformers, and variational autoencoders—are being used to integrate multi-omics data for genomic variant functional annotation, pharmacogenomics, and biomarker discovery. It frames the computational challenge of combining high-dimensional genomics, transcriptomics, epigenomics, and proteomics data into clinically actionable insights for precision medicine.

papers.title: Strategic roadmap for FAIR-compliant transcriptomic workflows: from technical challenges to bioinformatics democratization.
papers.abstract: This article draws on the authors' more than 17 years of experience in transcriptomic research, beginning with the introduction of high-throughput sequencing in Mexico in 2009. Here, we provide a critical review of bioinformatics pipelines for different RNA classes, ranging from small RNAs to long non-coding RNAs. Our analysis encompasses a range of scenarios, from de novo transcriptome assembly for organisms lacking a closely related and adequately annotated reference genome to differential expression analysis based on a well-annotated reference genome. By providing a comprehensive overview o
papers.summary: This review draws on the authors' 17+ years of transcriptomic research experience to critically assess bioinformatics pipelines for various RNA classes, from small RNAs to long non-coding RNAs. It covers scenarios ranging from de novo transcriptome assembly for poorly annotated organisms to differential expression analysis with well-annotated references, and proposes a strategic roadmap for FAIR-compliant workflows aimed at democratizing bioinformatics access.

papers.title: gTranslate: rapid and accurate translation table prediction for prokaryotic genomes.
papers.abstract: Bioinformatic tools often require the prediction of protein-coding genes to make inferences about prokaryotic genomes. Typically, the genetic code used for translating genes to proteins must be specified by the user based on the taxonomic classification of a genome assembly or, for some widely used tools, established using a heuristic rule based on gene coding densities. Manual specification is at best inconvenient, but more challenging is that many bioinformatic tools are applied before taxonomic classifications have been established making specifying the translation table impractical.
papers.summary: gTranslate is a new tool that predicts the correct genetic code (translation table) for prokaryotic genomes directly from sequence data, without requiring prior taxonomic classification. This addresses a common bottleneck in bacterial and archaeal genome annotation pipelines, where the translation table must otherwise be specified manually or inferred via crude heuristics. The tool aims to make gene prediction more accurate and automated.

papers.title: AI and computational methods for reconstructing cell-state-specific gene regulatory networks from single-cell transcriptome and chromatin accessibility data in cancer: methods, applications, and perspectives.
papers.abstract: Tumor heterogeneity is shaped by genetic, epigenetic, microenvironmental, and stochastic factors, among which cell-state-specific regulatory programs are a major determinant. Gene regulatory networks provide a systems-level model linking transcription factors, cis-regulatory elements, and target genes. Paired single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) and single-cell assay for transposase-accessible chromatin using sequencing (scATAC-seq) measure chromatin accessibility and gene expression in the same cell, offering a direct view of regulatory elements and transcriptional output; matched-but-unpai
papers.summary: This review surveys AI and computational methods for reconstructing cell-state-specific gene regulatory networks from single-cell RNA-seq and scATAC-seq data, with a focus on cancer. It covers approaches for both paired and matched-but-unpaired multiome data, discussing how these methods link transcription factors, cis-regulatory elements, and target genes to model tumor heterogeneity. The authors outline applications in cancer and offer perspectives on remaining challenges.

papers.title: Tissue-specific moderate DNA methylation alterations featuring hypomethylation in microRNA regulatory regions associated with advanced carotid atherosclerosis.
papers.abstract: DNA methylation is an important epigenetic mechanism involved in the regulation of gene expression, but its contribution to the regulation of microRNA genes in atherosclerosis remains poorly understood.
papers.journal: Frontiers in cell and developmental biology
papers.summary: This study examines DNA methylation changes in carotid atherosclerotic plaques, finding tissue-specific moderate alterations with hypomethylation particularly in microRNA regulatory regions in advanced disease. The results suggest that epigenetic dysregulation of microRNA genes may contribute to atherosclerosis progression.

papers.title: A methodology to identify a DNA methylation-based signature of prenatal air pollution exposure in the ECHO Cohort.
papers.abstract: Prenatal exposure to ambient air pollutants has been associated with adverse child health across different populations. In the absence of direct air pollution exposure measures, epigenetic biomarkers can serve as indicators of cumulative exposure. Previously, we developed a methodological pipeline to build a prediction model to distinguish infants highly exposed to air pollutants in utero based on DNA methylation in cord blood samples. Here, we test and refine this pipeline using data from multiple pregnancy cohort sites included in the Environmental influences on Child Health Outcomes (ECHO)
papers.summary: The authors test and refine a methodological pipeline for building a DNA methylation-based prediction model that distinguishes infants with high versus low prenatal air pollution exposure, using cord blood samples from multiple ECHO pregnancy cohorts. This work extends a prior single-cohort approach to a multi-site setting, aiming to establish epigenetic biomarkers as proxies for cumulative prenatal air pollution exposure when direct exposure measurements are unavailable.

papers.title: The double-edged sword of TOX: orchestrating T cell exhaustion and epigenetic remodeling in the tumor microenvironment.
papers.abstract: The capacity to profoundly change chromatin domains and in turn drive or inhibit gene expression makes chromatin modulators a powerful tool adopted to regulate crucial steps during development and cell lineage specification. These proteins can however be as well engaged to irreversibly reprogram cells toward pathological outcomes such as cancer. An example of such chromatin remodelers is the family of Thymocyte-selection associated high mobility box proteins (TOX), which has rather pleiotropic functions during development and in cancer. In light of the most recent findings, this review gives a
papers.summary: This review examines the dual role of TOX (thymocyte-selection associated HMG box) proteins as chromatin remodelers that orchestrate T cell exhaustion and epigenetic reprogramming within the tumor microenvironment. It highlights how TOX family members can drive both developmental lineage specification and pathological outcomes such as cancer, emphasizing their pleiotropic functions and potential as therapeutic targets.
